opening_message:
Ticket 1: Diana Cooper (employee ID E020) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E020.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Diana Cooper (E020) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee whose role (Engineer) owns the Source Code system, admin is permitted under policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB record for E020 shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have at most read (write requires advanced training, admin never permitted). Admin requested exceeds maximum, so grant read.
reason: Diana Cooper (E020) requested admin access to Source Code. There is conflicting employment-type information: the HR note lists full_time Engineer, while the Security note lists contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors are never permitted admin, and with basic training their maximum is read. Because the security record indicates contractor status and admin is explicitly prohibited for contractors, admin cannot be granted. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum allowed (read), so grant the maximum: read.
